paper_a.title: The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications

metadata.description: Paper A (Perelman) is the original Ricci-flow / entropy paper introducing F, W, lambda, mu, nu, reduced length, no-local-collapsing, pseudolocality, canonical neighborhoods, and thick-thin decomposition. Paper B (Kleiner-Lott) is an expository companion that follows Perelman's section numbering essentially verbatim, restates each definition / proposition / theorem, and supplies fully detailed proofs, plus material from Perelman's second paper (Ricci flow with surgery, Geometrization, Poincare). The pairing is best described as alternative-proof/elaboration: same theorems and proof strategies, but Kleiner-Lott rigorize each step. Almost every Perelman node has a near-verbatim counterpart in Kleiner-Lott, while Kleiner-Lott has a substantial body of paper-original surgery/geometrization material with no Perelman-paper-1 counterpart (because that material lives in Perelman's papers II and III, which are not part of this pair).

matches.explanation: Both define the Hamilton Ricci flow equation $\partial_t g = -2\Ric$ and both flag it as external (Hamilton 1982). Verbatim definition.
Same F-functional $\mathcal{F}(g,f) = \int_M (R + |\nabla f|^2) e^{-f} dV$. Identical formula.

Perelman defines breather generally (steady, shrinking, expanding via $\alpha$). Kleiner-Lott restate only the steady-breather case as DP399.4. Same conceptual object, B is a special case of A's definition.

Perelman's explicit Ricci-soliton definition has no standalone counterpart in the Kleiner-Lott extraction. Kleiner-Lott use solitons (steady, gradient-shrinking) but the extraction does not surface them as a Level-1 definition, treating them implicitly through PrP399.4.
Both define $\lambda(g)$ as $\inf \mathcal{F}(g,\cdot)$ subject to the unit-mass constraint, equivalently the lowest eigenvalue of $-4\triangle + R$. Same definition.
Same W-entropy functional with identical formula. Both note the unit-mass constraint.
Both define $\mu(g,\tau) = \inf \mathcal{W}$ under the constraint. Perelman additionally defines $\nu(g) = \inf_\tau \mu$; Kleiner-Lott's DP399.6 captures the same object.
Identical definition of locally collapsing Ricci flow at $T$ in terms of sequences $t_k \to T$ and balls $B(p_k,r_k)$ with $r_k^{-n} \Vol(B_k) \to 0$.

Identical definition of $\kappa$-noncollapsed metric on a scale, both labeled as Definition I.4.2. Note Kleiner-Lott also adds DP399.9, a parabolic variant they explicitly distinguish (RP399.3) and use in TP399.2.

Both define $\mathcal{L}$-length as $\int \sqrt{\tau}(R + |\dot\gamma|^2) d\tau$. Kleiner-Lott's DP399.10 also rolls in reduced length and reduced volume that Perelman defines as DP398.11 and DP398.12. This is a granularity mismatch: one B node groups three A nodes.

Reduced length $l(q,\tau) = L(q,\tau)/(2\sqrt{\tau})$ and reduced volume $\tilde V(\tau) = \int \tau^{-n/2} e^{-l} dq$ from Perelman are bundled into Kleiner-Lott's DP399.10 (Reduced length and reduced volume). Same objects, different node decomposition.

Perelman's DP398.13 defines $\kappa$-collapsed at $(x_0,t_0)$ on scale $r$ as a parabolic spacetime notion. Kleiner-Lott's DP399.9 is the parabolic $\kappa$-noncollapsed Ricci flow definition (its negation). They describe the same underlying parabolic concept but DP398.13 is the collapsed version on a single point and DP399.9 is the (non)collapsed version for the flow.

Both define $\phi$/$\Phi$-almost nonnegative curvature with $\Rm \ge -\phi(R) R$ (or $-\Phi(R)$). Kleiner-Lott use $\Phi$ vs Perelman $\phi$, and the precise normalization differs ($\phi(R) R$ vs $\Phi(R)$), but it is the same Hamilton-Ivey-style pinching condition.

Perelman's $\epsilon$-neck definition has no standalone Level-1 node in the Kleiner-Lott extraction; the concept is used implicitly inside DP399.15 (canonical neighborhood) and TP399.5 but not surfaced separately.
Asymptotic volume ratio $\cV$ has no standalone counterpart in the Kleiner-Lott extraction; used implicitly in their treatment of $\kappa$-solutions.

Perelman's upper bound on $\cF^m$ along its gradient flow (Proposition 1.2) has no standalone counterpart in the Kleiner-Lott extraction; that bound and its proof do appear in their notes but were not surfaced as Level-1 nodes.
Both state Theorem I.4.1 (No local collapsing I): for closed $M$ and finite $T$, the Ricci flow is not locally collapsing at $T$. Identical statement, hypotheses, and conclusions.

Perelman's proof of Proposition 1.2 (Cauchy-Schwarz argument bounding $\cF^m$) has no surfaced standalone proof node in Kleiner-Lott; the underlying Cauchy-Schwarz identity for $\cF$ is used in their notes (e.g. inside PP399.1 / I.1) but the corresponding upper-bound proposition itself was not surfaced in the Kleiner-Lott extraction (see PrP398.1 above).

Perelman's proof of $\bar\lambda$ monotonicity (PP398.2 proving ClP398.1) has no surfaced counterpart in Kleiner-Lott's extraction; their analogous proof PP399.2 establishes (unnormalized) $\lambda$ monotonicity, not $\bar\lambda$.
Perelman's proof of asymptotic-$\mu$ behavior (Section 3.1) is not surfaced as a standalone proof node in Kleiner-Lott's extraction.

Both prove TP398.1/TP399.1 by the same argument: build cutoff test functions $\Phi_k$ that drive $\mu(g(t_k), r_k^2) \to -\infty$, then use monotonicity of $\mu$ along the flow to contradict continuity at $t=0$. Kleiner-Lott (PP399.3) is the elaboration of Perelman's proof sketch (PP398.4).

Inner step DAGs for the no-local-collapsing-I proof match step-for-step. A's PSP398.4 (build degenerate test function) = B's PSP399.1 (set up $\Phi_k$). A's PSP398.5 (drive $\mu$ to $-\infty$) = B's PSP399.2 (bound $\mathcal{W} \to -\infty$). A's PSP398.6 (apply monotonicity to reach contradiction) = B's PSP399.3 + PSP399.4 (apply monotonicity, conclude). Kleiner-Lott split the conclude step out as a separate atom.

Both state No local collapsing II (Theorem I.7.3 / Theorem 8.2 in Perelman): given A and noncollapsing/curvature/volume hypotheses at $t=0$, the flow cannot be $\kappa(A)$-collapsed at later times in a large parabolic region. Same theorem; Kleiner-Lott package the parabolic noncollapsing definition slightly differently (DP399.9) but the result is the same.

Perelman's proof of Theorem 8.2 (PP398.5: maximum-principle on $h(y,t)$ involving $\bar L$) has no standalone proof node in the Kleiner-Lott extraction at this granularity, though the underlying argument is present in their I.7 / II.5 sections. Kleiner-Lott LP399.2 (Lemma II.5.2) reuses the same noncollapsing argument adapted to surgery.
Perelman's distance distortion lemma 8.3 has no surfaced Level-1 counterpart in the Kleiner-Lott extraction; it is used inside their I.7/I.8 proofs but not extracted as a node.

Both state the conjugate-heat localized differential Harnack identity $\square^* v = -2(T-t)|R_{ij} + \nabla_i\nabla_j f - g_{ij}/(2(T-t))|^2 u$, with $u = (4\pi(T-t))^{-n/2} e^{-f}$ and $v$ the entropy density. Perelman's Section 9.1 = Kleiner-Lott's Proposition I.9.1.

Perelman's four corollaries of Section 9 (monotonicity of $\min v/u$, $v \le 0$ for $\delta$-data, differential Harnack along curves, $f \le l$) have no surfaced Level-1 counterparts in Kleiner-Lott's extraction; they are used implicitly in their proof of pseudolocality but not surfaced as Level-1 corollaries.

Perelman's Corollary 4.2 ($\kappa$-noncollapsing of blow-up limits) has no standalone counterpart in the Kleiner-Lott extraction; the result is folded into their treatment of $\kappa$-solutions (DP399.11) and the canonical neighborhood theorem proof.

Pseudolocality theorem (Theorem I.10.1). Both state: for any $\alpha$ there exist $\delta, \epsilon$ such that under scalar curvature lower bound and almost-Euclidean isoperimetric inequality at $t=0$, $|Rm|(x,t) < \alpha t^{-1} + (\epsilon r_0)^{-2}$ holds in a parabolic neighborhood. Verbatim.

Both prove pseudolocality by the same contradiction argument: localize a bad $(\bar x, \bar t)$, build conjugate heat solution $u$ from a $\delta$-function and the corresponding $v$, derive a strictly negative upper bound on $\int_B v$, propagate to $t=0$, contradict the Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality. Kleiner-Lott PP399.4 is the elaborated version.

Inner step DAGs match one-for-one. PSP398.10 (point selection / Claim 1) = PSP399.5 (point-selection Claim 1). PSP398.11 ($v$-bound from $\delta$-data, Claim 3) = PSP399.6 + PSP399.7 (parabolic regions Claim 2 + negative $\int v$ bound Claim 3). PSP398.12 (cutoff h, propagate to $t=0$) overlaps with the cutoff in PSP399.8. PSP398.13 (contradict log-Sobolev) = the conclusion in PSP399.8.

Perelman's Theorem 10.3 (pseudolocality variant with volume hypothesis instead of isoperimetric inequality) has no standalone Level-1 node in Kleiner-Lott; it is a corollary of TP399.3 and is implicit in their treatment.
Perelman's lower volume bound from pseudolocality (Cor 10.2) is not surfaced as a Level-1 node in Kleiner-Lott, though they use it inside the canonical neighborhood and surgery arguments.
Perelman's $\kappa$-noncollapsing under almost-Euclidean isoperimetry (Cor 10.4) has no surfaced Level-1 counterpart in Kleiner-Lott.

Existence of the asymptotic gradient shrinking soliton for $\kappa$-solutions (Proposition I.11.2): blow down by $\bar\tau_i \to \infty$ at $q(\bar\tau_i)$ with $l(q,\bar\tau) \le n/2$, extract a non-flat gradient shrinking soliton. Same proposition.
Perelman's proof of Proposition 11.2 is not surfaced as a separate proof node in Kleiner-Lott's extraction; the argument lives in their I.11 section.
Inner proof_steps for blow-down to gradient shrinking soliton are not surfaced in Kleiner-Lott's extraction at the proof_step granularity.
Perelman's Corollary 11.3 (2D $\kappa$-solutions are round spheres) is not surfaced as a Level-1 node in Kleiner-Lott; it appears inside their classification ClP399.8.
Perelman's $\cV = 0$ for ancient $\kappa$-solutions (Prop 11.4) is not extracted as a Level-1 node in Kleiner-Lott; folded into compactness TP399.4.

Volume-decay, curvature-from-volume, and necks-outside-compact-set corollaries of Perelman Section 11 are not surfaced as Level-1 nodes in Kleiner-Lott; they live inside their canonical-neighborhood and $\kappa$-solution machinery.

Compactness of 3D $\kappa$-solutions (Theorem I.11.7). Perelman states it for noncompact ancient solutions; Kleiner-Lott TP399.4 gives the standard pointed-compactness statement for normalized $\kappa$-solutions. Same theorem under the standard normalization.
Perelman's proof of Theorem 11.7 (long-distance separation, bounded curvature at $t=0$) is not surfaced as a separate proof node in Kleiner-Lott; it is part of their I.11 narrative.
Inner proof_steps for compactness of ancient solutions are not surfaced in Kleiner-Lott at this granularity.
Perelman's proof of $\cV = 0$ via trichotomy on asymptotic scalar curvature ratio is not surfaced as a separate proof node in Kleiner-Lott.
Inner proof_steps for the Prop 11.4 trichotomy are not extracted in Kleiner-Lott at this granularity.

Canonical neighborhood theorem (I.12.1): given $\epsilon, \kappa, \Phi$, there exists $r_0$ such that any high-curvature spacetime point ($R \ge r_0^{-2}$) of a $\Phi$-almost-nonnegative-curvature, $\kappa$-noncollapsed Ricci flow is, after rescaling, $\epsilon$-close to a $\kappa$-solution. Same theorem; both attribute it to I.12.1.

Both prove the canonical neighborhood theorem by contradiction with point selection, blow-up limit construction, and backward extension via Hamilton compactness. Same proof outline; PP399.5 is the elaborated version.

Inner step DAGs match almost one-for-one. PSP398.17 (point selection / setup contradiction) = PSP399.9 (point selection Step 1). PSP398.18 (Claim 1: local curvature bound) and PSP398.19 (Claim 2: cylindrical structure) overlap with PSP399.10 (build limit time slice Step 2). PSP398.20 (smooth limit + backward extension) = PSP399.11 + PSP399.12 (extend backwards Step 3, conclude Step 4).

Curvature bound at fixed time / Later scalar curvature bounds on bigger balls (Theorem I.12.2). Both state: for any $A$ there exists $K(A)$ such that under appropriate hypotheses including those of Theorem 8.2 / TP399.2 with $r_0 = 1$, $R(x,1) \le K$ for $\dist_1(x,x_0) < A$. Same theorem.

Curvature bound from volume hypothesis / Earlier scalar curvature bounds on smaller balls (Theorem I.12.3). Same theorem in both papers; the past/future role swap of TP399.7 is the standard restatement.
Perelman's Cor 12.4 (volume bound from sectional curvature minimum) is not surfaced as a Level-1 node in Kleiner-Lott; it follows from TP399.6/TP399.7.

Thick-thin decomposition (Theorem I.13.1). Both state existence of $T(w), \bar\rho(w), K(w)$ such that for large $t$, $M = M_{thick} \cup M_{thin}$ with controlled curvature/volume on $M_{thick}$ in scale $\sqrt{t}$. Identical statement.

Perelman's Claim 2.3 ($\bar\lambda$ monotonicity along Ricci flow when nonpositive) has no surfaced Level-1 counterpart in Kleiner-Lott; their PrP399.3 is the unnormalized $\lambda$-monotonicity, which is a relative.
Perelman's asymptotic-$\mu$ claim (Section 3.1) has no surfaced Level-1 counterpart in Kleiner-Lott.

Monotonicity formula for $\cF$ (1.4) has no surfaced equation node in Kleiner-Lott; the formula is the conclusion of PrP399.1's first variation but Kleiner-Lott package it as a proposition rather than an equation.
Monotonicity formula for $\cW$ (3.4) has no surfaced equation node in Kleiner-Lott; used implicitly in TP399.1.
$\mathcal{L}$-geodesic equation (7.2) is used in Kleiner-Lott's I.7 sections but not surfaced as an equation node.
Differential inequality for reduced length $l$ (7.13)/(7.14) is used but not surfaced as a Level-1 node in Kleiner-Lott.

Perelman's algorithmic sketch of Hamilton's surgery procedure (Section 13.2) is the high-level surgery idea; Kleiner-Lott DP399.18 is the rigorous Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff definition that formalizes it. Same procedure, A is sketch, B is the formal version. Cross-type (algorithm vs definition) match justified by the conceptual identity.

Perelman's open problem (boundedness of normalized curvature for nonsingular flows) is paper-original speculation with no Kleiner-Lott counterpart; Kleiner-Lott does not surface this open problem in their extraction.
Perelman's conjecture on uniqueness of noncompact 3D ancient solutions (Bryant soliton) has no surfaced counterpart in Kleiner-Lott, though they discuss the same topic in I.11.9.

Kleiner-Lott surface the first variation of $\mathcal{F}$ as a separate proposition + proof (PrP399.1, PP399.1). Perelman states the formula in passing in his Section 1 but the Authomathics extraction does not surface it as a Level-1 node, so this is a Kleiner-Lott-only contribution at the extraction level.

Kleiner-Lott explicitly state existence and uniqueness of the $\mathcal{F}$-minimizer (PrP399.2). Perelman uses this fact implicitly (defining DP398.5 via $\inf$) but does not state it as a separate proposition; not extracted in paper A.

Kleiner-Lott surface the monotonicity of $\lambda$ under Ricci flow as PrP399.3 with proof PP399.2. Perelman states this in Section 1.2 but the extraction did not surface it as a Level-1 node, only Cl398.1 (the closely related $\bar\lambda$ monotonicity).

Kleiner-Lott surface the steady breather / gradient steady soliton rigidity as PrP399.4. Perelman states the analogous fact in his Section 2 but the Authomathics extraction did not surface it as a Level-1 node.

Kleiner-Lott explicitly define $\kappa$-solution (Definition I.11.1) as a Level-1 node. Perelman uses the concept throughout his Section 11 but the extraction did not surface it as a standalone definition; the conditions appear only as the assumptions of TP398.5/PrP398.3 etc.
Universal $\kappa_0$ (Proposition I.11.9) is surfaced in Kleiner-Lott but not extracted as a standalone node from Perelman, despite Perelman discussing the same fact in his Section 11.9.

Kleiner-Lott incorporate material from Perelman's second paper (Ricci flow with surgery): standard solution, Ricci flow with surgery, canonical neighborhood (II.4.1), $\Phi$-pinching, a priori assumptions, normalized initial condition. None of these have a counterpart in Perelman paper 1, since this material lives in Perelman's papers II/III which are not part of this pair.
Lemmas II.5.2 / II.5.3 (forcing $\mathcal{L}_+$ to be large; noncollapsing in presence of surgery) are from Perelman's second paper; no counterpart in paper A.
Existence of Ricci flow with surgery for all time (Proposition II.5.1) and its proof are from Perelman's second paper; no counterpart in paper A.

Inner proof_steps for Prop II.5.1 (induction setup, noncollapsing in presence of surgery, canonical neighborhood, surgeries do not accumulate, conclude induction) are from paper B's surgery section; no counterpart in paper A.

Thin-part-is-graph-manifold theorems (II.7.4 first/second versions) and the corollary that the thin part of a long-time Ricci flow with surgery is a graph manifold are from Perelman paper II / Shioya-Yamaguchi; no counterpart in paper A.
Incompressibility of cuspidal tori is from Perelman paper II; no counterpart in paper A.

Geometrization Conjecture from Ricci flow with surgery — main result of Perelman paper II + III, surfaced by Kleiner-Lott. Paper A (Perelman I) does not state Geometrization as a theorem, only points toward it; the result lives in his second/third papers.
Poincare Conjecture corollary and its proof from Claims 1-4. This is the headline result of Perelman papers II/III, not paper I. Paper A does not state Poincare in the extracted nodes.

Kleiner-Lott's eight introductory Claims (singular set structure, surgery, surgeries do not accumulate, finite extinction, hyperbolic limit, thin part graph manifold, $\kappa$-solution model, classification of $\kappa$-solutions) summarize Perelman papers II/III. Paper A does not state these claims at the extraction level.
